summary: Guest argues that US natural gas (NG1) is down this year while LNG prices in the rest of the world are up 100-200%, making America relatively advantaged as natural gas is the dominant input for US electricity and manufacturing. A closed Strait of Hormuz reinforces this relative US advantage.
quote: NG1. It is down this year. The input cost for electricity in the rest of the world...LNG is a very important one, and it's up 100%, 200%. And so the Strait of Hormuz is absolutely bad for everyone, but relatively good for America.
